### Observed differences

- The dominant shift is a swap between two groups of activities. In the later window, A21, A22, A23 and A24 each appear in only about 28 in 100 traces, down from about 83 in 100, while A25, A26, A27 and A28 each appear in about 73 in 100, up from about 18 in 100. - A04 also recedes: it appears in about 16 in 100 later traces, down from about 55 in 100. Smaller rises for A02 (about 5 to 14 in 100) and A08 (about 4 to 12 in 100) rest on few traces. [OCC002, OCC001, OCC003]
- Routing changed at two points. At A20, the share of outgoing transitions to A24 fell from about 83% to 27%, while the share to A28 rose from 17% to 72%. At A31, the share to A04 fell from about 52% to 6%, while the share to A19 rose from 45% to 84%, and A31 now rarely co-occurs with A04 at all (about 55 to 16 in 100 traces). [DIR003, DIR004, REL011]
- A04's own outgoing transitions, previously about 87% to A19, now spread over many targets (A19 about 32%, A16 about 15%, A35 about 12%); this profile is based on fewer observations later (34 versus 120 transitions). [DIR001]
- A19 and A20 now usually appear without the old block: co-occurrence with A21–A24 fell from about 83 to 28 in 100 traces, with A19/A20 alone in about 72 in 100. [REL013, REL021]
- A19 and A20 now usually precede the new block: co-occurrence with A25–A28 rose from about 18 to 73 in 100, with A19/A20 first in about 71–73 of those; A31 and A32 also now typically precede A25–A28. [REL017, REL025, REL062, REL071]
- The new block holds together — A25–A28 now typically occur in the same trace (about 73 in 100, versus about 27 before, when neither usually appeared) — while A04's ties weakened across the board: with A19/A20 co-occurrence fell from about 55 to 16 in 100, and with A21–A24 the typical outcome is now that neither appears (about 62 in 100). [REL059, REL064, REL001, REL003, REL007]
- Distances along the new path tightened: A31 reaches A19 in 1 step in about 84 in 100 later traces (previously split between 1 and 2 steps), A20 in 2 steps in about 80 (previously mostly 3), and A28 in 3 steps in about 82 (previously mostly 4). Lag results around A04 rest on only 8–17 later observations. [LAG007, LAG008, LAG010, LAG001, LAG002, LAG003]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility that the process was rerouted: the alternative block A21–A24, which in the earlier window typically ran after A19/A20 behind the segment through A04, was largely set aside in favour of the block A25–A28, and the A04 segment was largely bypassed, with A31 now typically continuing directly to A19 and A20 and onward to A25–A28. In the later window A21–A24 appear in about 28 in 100 traces (down from 83), A25–A28 in about 73 (up from 18), and A04 in about 16 (down from 55). [DIR003, DIR004, REL017, OCC004, OCC008, OCC002]

The support is direct and consistent: the successor shares at A20 and A31 shift exactly where the participation swings predict, and the relational evidence places A19/A20 and A31/A32 before A25–A28 in the large majority of later traces. [DIR003, DIR004, REL017, REL062] In total 99 evidence items qualified, many times the roughly 1 expected for an unchanged process at these thresholds, and each item's difference exceeded about 199 of 200 random re-splits of the pooled data; note that the many relation items describe overlapping pairs of the same underlying behaviour and are not independent confirmations. [OCC001, DIR001, POS001, REL001, LAG001]

Limitations: with 200 traces per window, a difference in the mix of case variants between the windows could produce the same pattern without any change to the process, and the evidence cannot rule this out. The old path is used less often rather than shown removed — A21–A24 still appear in about 28 in 100 later traces and A04 in about 16 — and the small rises for A02 and A08 and the rerouting at A06 rest on few observations. [OCC004, OCC002, OCC001, DIR002]
